liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Sugaree** (2 reviews): Sugaree runs over fourteen minutes; reviewer ranks it the best they have heard; Sugaree is long and loping, typical of the era [14][19]
- **Saint of Circumstance** (2 reviews): Early Saint of Circumstance has lyrics noticeably different from the eventual version; the music is similar but still tentative; The early Lost Sailor/Saint pairing has different lyrics and feel from later versions, and is worth hearing [17][19]
- **Jack Straw** (1 review): Reviewer hears the opener as extended, noodling guitar playing from Jerry [14]
- **Lost Sailor** (1 review): Lost Sailor > Saint of Circumstance > Deal was widely read as a coded message about the band's drug use, which reviewer says was untrue [22]
- **Around & Around** (1 review): Around & Around closes the set with very little energy, to this reviewer's disappointment [19]
- **Shakedown Street** (1 review): Reviewer treats the Shakedown Street encore as the capstone of the night [14]

## The recordings

- **gd1979-09-04.009452.sbd.clugston.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 169 min [1]
- **gd1979-09-04.nak700.glassberg.wise.117776.flac1644**: source not stated; 20 songs; 174 min; rated 1.5/5 by 2 [2]. Said about its sound: This transfer lacks the whistle-blowing fan heard in the first set of the other source, and has more gain [2]
- **gd1979-09-04.sbd.miller.79747.flac16**: soundboard; 19 songs; 170 min; rated 3.53/5 by 15 [3]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds this soundboard mix remarkably clear, with every instrument distinct; Reviewer notes some sound problems on the soundboard, though milder than another listener claimed; Uploader calls this soundboard poor, with many pitch problems [3][15][16]
- **gd79-09-04.glassberg.unknown.8379.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 19 songs; 171 min; rated 3.75/5 by 4 [4]. Said about its sound: A noisy neighbor near the taper spoiled the first set, but the rest is a stellar audience recording from the sweet spot; Front-of-board-style audience recording; a whistle-blowing fan annoys through the first set but is gone in the second [11][12]
- **gd1979-09-04.156349.senn441.senn421.blend.eaton.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 19 songs; 174 min [5]

## Around the show

- Reviewer recalls the show falling just as summer ended, with two more Madison Square Garden nights still to come [13]
- Lost Sailor and Saint here show an early stage of a pairing that later evolved into a settled piece [17]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1979-09-04.009452.sbd.clugston.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Patching / CD Mastering by Scott Clugston EAC'ed / SHN'ed by Scott Clugston 4/16/02; source: Master Soundboard Cassette > Reel to Reel > PCM > CDR [1]. Also: Barry Glassberg's master audience cassette, recorded with Nakamichi CM700 mics, patches this soundboard release; Scott Clugston did patching and mastering; Audience source fills the opening seconds of Jack Straw, all of Looks Like Rain, and short sections of Minglewood, China Cat and Wharf Rat [1]
- **gd1979-09-04.nak700.glassberg.wise.117776.flac1644**: taped by Jim Wise and Barry Glassberg; source: Nakamichi 700s > Sony TC-158, 14th row recording by Barry Glassberg. Transferred MAC > CDR by Jim Wise (c2000) CDR > EAC > TLH > FLAC 1644 tagged (Dec 2011) [2]. Also: This Glassberg Nakamichi 700 transfer has a first set differing entirely from the version on archive ID 8379; the second set matches [2]
- **gd1979-09-04.sbd.miller.79747.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Cassette -> Reel -> Dat -> PCM -> CD [3]. Also: Front-of-board, fourteenth-row Nakamichi 700 cassette master supplies the start of China Cat Sunflower on this soundboard [3]
- **gd79-09-04.glassberg.unknown.8379.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Recording: NAK 700's [4]
- **gd1979-09-04.156349.senn441.senn421.blend.eaton.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Rob Eaton for the recording, as well as the transfer and harddrive; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Rob Eaton's Master Audience Cassettes; (2) Sennheiser 441 (left + right) + (1) Sennheiser 421 (center) blend > Nakamichi 550 [5]. Also: Bob Wagner's Nakamichi 700 source supplies some crowd, the start of Jack Straw, and a brief patch in Space [5]

## Art and photos

- Poster by www.gratefulseconds.com: [Madison Square Garden Took One Million Souls During Grateful Dead's 52-Show 15-Year Run, 1979-1994](http://www.gratefulseconds.com/2017/08/madison-square-garden-took-one-million.html) [24]
